Check and Rewrite the \(x) Lambda Functions

Source: R/lambda_check.R
lambda_check.Rd

Checks that the anonymous functions are written function(x) and not with the \(x) shorthand (e.g., function(x) x * 2 and not \(x) x * 2). Prints a table of the reported lambdas and returns a corrected version of the function.

Usage

lambda_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Function to check, written without quotes and brackets (e.g., fun1 or pkg::fun1).

export

Single logical value. If TRUE, the corrected function is written into the <name>_safer.R file of out_path instead of being returned (e.g., fun1_safer.R for x = fun1 or x = pkg::fun1), as fun1_safer <- function(...), which base::source() recreates. Nothing is written if nothing has to be corrected, but an error is returned if the file already exists, or if x is not a function name (e.g., function(x){x} or FUN_LIST$fun).

out_path

Single character string: path of an existing folder where the file is written. Required when export is TRUE; otherwise not used, but a non-NULL value must still be a single non-empty character string. NULL by default.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

The corrected function, which keeps the environment of x, or NULL, invisibly, if nothing has to be corrected or if export is TRUE.

A message is also printed: a table with one row per reported lambda (column 1: line number; column 2: symbol; column 3: code of the line), or a sentence saying that everything seems clean.

Details

Source references: line 1 is the line of the function keyword. The \(x) writing is only kept in a function that carries its source references (attribute srcref), e.g., parsed with keep.source = TRUE (base::parse(), base::source()). Functions created with options(keep.source = FALSE) (default of Rscript) and functions of installed packages (e.g., saferDev::colons_check) have none: their deparsed code shows function(x), so that nothing can be reported.

Reported: the lambdas written \(x), like \(x) x * 2, \(x){ x } or \() base::mean(1:3), wherever they are written in the function. In the printed table, the symbol is \() when the formals of the lambda span several lines.

Not reported: the standard function(x) writing (an unbraced body like function(x) x is reported by curly_bracket_check()). A \( inside a string, a comment or a backquoted name is ignored.

Correction: the \ of each reported lambda is replaced by function (e.g., \(x) x * 2 becomes function(x) x * 2). The rest of the code, comments, indentation and lambda bodies included, is unchanged.

See also

The code checkers of saferDev, in the recommended order of use: super_assign_check, lambda_check, colons_check, all_args_here, curly_bracket_check, true_false_check, for_loop_nb_check (see vignette("saferDev")).

Author

Gael Millot

Examples

# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/lambda_check.html
# The \(x) writing is only kept in a function carrying its source references: hence
# keep.source = TRUE, and srcfile left empty (srcfile = NULL would remove them).
code1 <- "function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = function(y){ y * 2 }) }"
fun1 <- base::eval(expr = base::parse(file = "", n = NULL, text = code1, prompt = "?",
    keep.source = TRUE, srcfile = , encoding = "unknown"), envir = , enclos = )
saferDev::lambda_check(x = fun1, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # nothing to correct: NULL returned, invisibly
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::lambda_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
code2 <- "function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \\(y){ y * 2 }) }"
fun2 <- base::eval(expr = base::parse(file = "", n = NULL, text = code2, prompt = "?",
    keep.source = TRUE, srcfile = , encoding = "unknown"), envir = , enclos = )
fun2_safer <- saferDev::lambda_check(x = fun2, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL,
    safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # lambda writing reported
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME LAMBDA FUNCTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN function():
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 1	\(y)		function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \(y){ y * 2 }) }
#> 
fun2_safer # corrected function
#> function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = function(y){ y * 2 }) }
#> <environment: 0x6235c1d0ef78>
# A backslash followed by ( in a string, a raw string, a comment or a backquoted name
# is not a lambda writing: not reported, not modified.
code3 <- base::paste0(
    "function(x){ y <- \"the text \\\\(x) is inside a string\" ; ",
    "z <- r\"(raw \\(x))\" ; # a \\(x) in a comment\n    `\\\\(w)` <- 1 ; x }",
    collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE
)
fun3 <- base::eval(expr = base::parse(file = "", n = NULL, text = code3, prompt = "?",
    keep.source = TRUE, srcfile = , encoding = "unknown"), envir = , enclos = )
saferDev::lambda_check(x = fun3, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # nothing to correct: NULL returned, invisibly
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::lambda_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
# Write the corrected function in the fun2_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(check = FALSE), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::lambda_check(x = fun2, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME LAMBDA FUNCTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN function():
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 1	\(y)		function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \(y){ y * 2 }) }
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpQNRq2A/dir11045221b37e/fun2_safer.R
#> 
base::unlink(x = tempo_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = FALSE, expand = TRUE) # folder removed
